statement: AFT (Procedure) Rules 2008 Form III is attributed to 'rule 17'. The source prints 'rule 27'. So the printed_title, prescribing_provision, requirement_language_as_printed and version_amendment_history of FF-AFTPR08-F3 all state a rule number that is not printed in the source. This breaks the 'nothing invented / as printed' rule. The fuzzy OCR match accepted the OCR string 'rule :l 7'.
evidence: AFTPR08-C7 (sha256 590cf7cd...e0e317), PDF p.46 page image: 'FORM III (see rule 27) APPLICATION FOR THE REGISTRATION OF A CLERK'. PDF p.37 page image: heading '27. Registration of legal practitioner's clerk.' PDF p.38: sub-rule (3) 'shall make an application to the Registrar in Form III'. spec_forms.py lines 770-775 hard-code 'rule 17'.
requested_action: Correct FF-AFTPR08-F3 to r.27 (heading at p.37, sub-rule (3) at p.38) and title '(see rule 27)'. Then rebuild. Add a guard so that any digit token in an OCR-mode anchor or title must match EXACT, or be visually confirmed, before it is accepted.

statement: Form H (Appendix V) is classified STATUTORY_PRESCRIBED / MANDATORY_FORM_WORDING. Its provision, AR 169, is permissive: 'may, if he thinks fit, by a warrant in one of the forms in Appendix V'. This contradicts the README rule that STATUTORY_PRESCRIBED applies only where a provision says the form 'shall' be used. It is also treated differently from AFT Form II, a comparable 'may' case, which was given PERMISSIVE_ATTACHMENT_FORM_PRESCRIBED.
evidence: AR54-IC p.191, AR 169 text, verified. Register row FC-AR54-APPV-FH~MML2~1. Its own outstanding_uncertainties already notes 'AR 169 is permissive'.
requested_action: Either reclassify Form H to a conditional or permissive category, or restate the README rule as 'form wording prescribed if the instrument is used' and apply it the same way to Form H and AFT Form II.

statement: AR 4(1) also says that 'a deviation from such forms shall not, by reason only of such deviation, render invalid any charge, warrant, order, proceedings...'. This applies to every Appendix form, including those covered by a specific 'shall' rule (rr.22, 23(6), 26(3), 27, 166, 167, 170A, 170B, 171, 179(5A), 190). Rows labelled MANDATORY_FORM_WORDING do not record this. The boilerplate 'Form status under AR 4 is permissive unless a specific rule uses shall' is an interpretive proposition that no held source prints, and it is attached even to rows whose rule does say 'shall'.
evidence: AR54-GAZ p.2 and AR54-IC p.2, AR 4(1) text, verified. Boilerplate appears in outstanding_uncertainties of the Army Rules rows.
requested_action: Add AR 4(1) as a related provision on every Army Rules appendix row. Replace the boilerplate with a neutral statement, e.g. 'interaction between the specific rule and AR 4(1) not determined; legal review'. Do not imply a hierarchy.

statement: 22 families take MML 2 (UNVERIFIED_MANUAL, undated) as PRIMARY although an official Gazette copy (1954 Gazette and/or the 1993 S.R.O. 17(E)) is held. Their field inventories therefore reproduce MML text. Example: the 'Findings' column of the Appendix III Part II offence report is EXACT in MML 2 only. It is WEAK (0.714) in the 1954 Gazette and in both MML DOC transcriptions.
evidence: FORM_FIELDS.csv FF-AR54-APPIII-P2#F13. AR54-GAZ p.72 page image shows the columns Place and date / Offence / Plea / Names of Witnesses / Punishment awarded / Signature... / Date of entry / Remarks, with no 'Findings' column. 5 field rows are NOT_FOUND or WEAK in the 1954 copy.
requested_action: Either make the official copy the primary where it is held (visual check required for OCR scans), or label each such field set 'MML 2 version (unverified)' at family level. Put every field that is NOT_FOUND or WEAK in an official copy into the conflict queue.

statement: MML-only status is flagged only in free text. 32 families have no non-MML occurrence. Nine of them are classified STATUTORY_PRESCRIBED: DPP Sch. I Forms I-III and Sch. II, ISL Forms A-D and the Indian Tolls Pass. For ISL and Tolls even the prescribing rule text is quoted from MML vol 3. fidelity_state reads TRANSCRIBED. SUMMARY.json has no MML-only count. The README headline lists these instruments without qualification.
evidence: Register rows with source_key MML3 for the ISL and ITR families. DPPR53-C7 holds the DPP rule text but no schedules (COV-23). The evidence class and uncertainties mention UNVERIFIED_MANUAL, but there is no structured flag.
requested_action: Add a structured family-level field such as evidence_basis=MML_ONLY_UNVERIFIED or official_copy_held=NO, plus a SUMMARY count. Qualify the authority candidate for ISL and ITR as 'per unverified MML text'. State the 32/67 split in the README headline.

statement: Coverage state INSPECTED_NO_FORMS_FOUND is given on the strength of heading-pattern or text-layer scans only, with no visual inspection. This covers MML-AA-PDF, MML1-DOC, AA50-IC, AFT07-IC, C5 amendment gazettes (OCR) and the c7 derived texts. One of these is the AFT (Procedure) Amendment Rules 2011: its c7 text is about 3 KB of largely garbled bilingual OCR, yet it is marked INSPECTED_NO_FORMS_FOUND. The same text appears to insert r.12A (affidavit supporting applications), which bears on AFT Form I companion documents and was not compared.
evidence: SOURCE_COVERAGE COV-13, 15, 20, 26-52, 60-63. git c7@ad77758d data/text/rules-aft-amendment-procedure-rules-2011.txt (201 lines; Hindi OCR noise; tail shows '12A.—Every application under rule 8 ... shall be supported by an affidavit'). Blueprint section 3: 'OCR alone cannot establish fidelity'.
requested_action: Downgrade these rows to PARTIAL, or add an explicit method-limitation state. For FF-AFTPR08-F1, record the 2011 amendment as an unexamined dependency: name it, do not interpret it.

statement: Coverage of service scope is not stated honestly enough. The 'Army-first scope of this cycle' appears only in one coverage-row note and in code comments, not in the README or SUMMARY. Air Force and Navy subordinate instruments, for example Air Force Rules 1969 and the Navy discipline regulations, are listed neither as NOT_HELD known-needed sources nor as explicitly out of scope. A reader could take the 67 families as the military-law form universe.
evidence: build_forms_registry.py lines 411 and 521. README 'Not done' list. COV-64..83 contain Army/TA/DPP/AFT items only.
requested_action: State the scope in the README and SUMMARY. Add NOT_HELD or OUT_OF_SCOPE_THIS_CYCLE rows for Air Force and Navy rule-level instruments, without asserting what they contain.

statement: Oath rows use a single template requirement quote: 'in one of the following forms or in such other form to the same purport'. This is verbatim for AR 9, 45, 109 and 140, but not for AR 46, which reads 'in such of the following forms as shall be appropriate, or in such other form to the same purport...'. AR 140 is also conditional ('if so required by the Act'), and the quote omits this.
requested_action: Use a verbatim per-rule quote in requirement_language_as_printed.

statement: Pinpoint precision is weak in several rows. AR 22 should be AR 22(3)(a): it is one limb of an 'or' choice. Form I (Appendix V) leads with the AR 170A(1) death-warrant quote, but the operative text is AR 170B(1)(b), 'shall... obtain the custody... by issuing a warrant in one of the forms in Appendix V'. The SGCM status label is PERMISSIVE_USE_AR4, although its quoted provision is AR 151(1) ('may be convened... in accordance with the form').
evidence: AR54-IC p.38, p.192 and p.182, verified.
requested_action: Tighten the pinpoints and quotes. Consider a status value for permissive use under a specific rule.

statement: The locator ranges for DOC-derived alternates are capped at start+400 lines. 19 occurrences hit the cap, and some run past end of file. Example: FC-AR54-APPV-FL~MML-AR-DOC~1 is given as L5806-6206, but the file has 5823 lines and Form L ends at about L5821. Cross-copy presence for generic labels in these ranges can be a false positive.
evidence: The register DOC_DERIVED_LINE rows where end-start=400. repro1/MML vol 2(AR).doc.lines.txt.
requested_action: Bound each range by the next form heading or by EOF. Mark capped ranges. Exclude generic labels from cross-copy scoring, or treat them as weak.

statement: Field 'verbatim' checks are whole-word matches on normalised text (case and punctuation stripped) within a page range. Many labels are generic ('Name', 'Unit', 'Dated', 'Signed', 'versus'). The R46 A-D sub-forms share pp.78-80, so their labels are not localised to a single sub-form.
evidence: Reviewer sample of 40 field rows (lowest sha256('C12-FORMS-REV'+field_id)): 39 are raw-verbatim on the cited pages. 1 (FF-AFTPR08-F1#F17) matches only after normalisation because of an OCR quote mark. None was invented.
requested_action: In the README, describe the method as 'normalised whole-word'. For template use, add per-form text boundaries (bbox or line spans).

statement: DPP Schedule II (a document list under r.33(3)) is typed STATUTORY_PRESCRIBED. r.33(3) prescribes documents that must accompany a report, not the wording of a form.
requested_action: Consider OTHER_OR_UNDETERMINED, or a document-list authority type. Keep MANDATORY_DOCUMENT_LIST as the status.

statement: Form-level sample: 15 families (lowest sha256('C12-FORMS-REV'+form_family_id)), 37 occurrences. Every anchor is present within its cited page or line range. All titles match apart from WSG-R01. All prescribing provisions are located as cited. All status classifications in the sample are defensible except AFT Form III (wrong rule number). Statutory set: 42/42 provisions were located. 40 contain 'shall' (some conditional). AR 169 (Form H) says 'may' (WSG-R02). AFT r.4(4) (Form II) says 'may attach', which is disclosed. For the ISL and Tolls rules, 'shall' is confirmed only in the unverified MML vol 3.
